# x402 Canary Live Base Transaction Verifier

Canonical URL: https://canary.0x402.sh/
Network: Base mainnet (`eip155:8453`)
Asset: native Base USDC (`0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913`, 6 decimals)
Evidence core commit: `3ead8680d764ecbafe0739865f3789f8928f0fa6`

x402 Canary performs an on-demand, transaction-only observation through two
server-pinned, read-only Base RPC origins. A caller supplies a public transaction
hash, never an RPC endpoint, wallet, signature, authorization, operation URL, or
payment instruction.

The live result verifies bounded public receipt and native-USDC EIP-3009 log facts.
It does not prove intended x402 terms, HTTP delivery, business effect, retry safety,
provider consensus truth, or external reality.

## Live transaction route

### GET /api/base-transaction?transactionHash=0x<64-lowercase-hex>

This route is strict GET-only; HEAD and OPTIONS return HTTP 405. The query must
contain exactly one `transactionHash` field. The value must be
`0x` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Duplicate fields,
array values, extra fields, whitespace, a request body, and caller-selected RPC
configuration are rejected.

The browser calls this same-origin route only after local shape validation. It
does not automatically retry or poll.

Successful evidence classifications return HTTP 200 with exactly these top-level
fields:

- `schemaVersion`: `"0.1"`.
- `kind`: `"public_base_transaction_verification"`.
- `checkedAt`: canonical UTC ISO 8601 observation time.
- `networkId`: `"eip155:8453"`.
- `transactionHash`: canonical lowercase transaction hash.
- `status`: one of the seven classifications below.
- `receipt`: canonical receipt summary or `null`.
- `finalizedAnchor`: shared finalized Base anchor or `null`.
- `sourceAgreement`: configured-source count, agreeing-source count, and quorum.
- `confirmations`: non-negative integer.
- `settlementCount`: total qualifying event-pair count.
- `settlements`: at most 32 sanitized native-USDC EIP-3009 event pairs.
- `truncated`: whether additional pairs were omitted.
- `reasons`: sorted sanitized reason codes.
- `observationHash`: content hash of the private core observation.
- `assurance`: fixed observation scope and trust model.
- `capabilities`: fixed execution and target-selection controls.
- `privacy`: public-hash transport and persistence facts.
- `limitations`: fixed false proof claims.

`receipt` is either `null` or exactly:

```json
{
  "transactionHash": "0x<64-lowercase-hex>",
  "blockHash": "0x<64-lowercase-hex>",
  "blockNumber": "canonical-decimal-string",
  "status": "success-or-reverted"
}
```

`finalizedAnchor` is either `null` or exactly:

```json
{
  "blockNumber": "canonical-decimal-string",
  "blockHash": "0x<64-lowercase-hex>",
  "blockTimestamp": "canonical-decimal-string"
}
```

`sourceAgreement` has this exact typed shape:

```typescript
{
  configured: 2;
  agreeing: 0 | 1 | 2;
  quorum: "unanimous";
}
```

`agreeing` is `2` only when both configured observations agree on the relevant
facts. A pending split may report `1`; a contradiction may report `0`. The
unanimous policy remains fixed even when the observed agreement count is below
quorum.

Each `settlements` entry is exactly:

```json
{
  "from": "0x<40-lowercase-hex>",
  "to": "0x<40-lowercase-hex>",
  "valueAtomic": "positive-canonical-decimal-string",
  "nonce": "0x<64-lowercase-hex>",
  "authorizationUsedLogIndex": 4,
  "transferLogIndex": 5
}
```

The two log indexes must be adjacent. `valueAtomic` is an exact integer in
six-decimal USDC atomic units and must not be converted through a floating-point
number.

`assurance` is exactly:

```json
{
  "scope": "fixed_source_base_receipt_and_native_usdc_eip3009_events",
  "sourceIdentity": "server_pinned_origins",
  "finality": "shared_finalized_block_hash",
  "quorum": "unanimous",
  "externalTruthProven": false
}
```

`capabilities` is exactly:

```json
{
  "fixedSourceBaseVerificationEnabled": true,
  "callerSelectedTransactionHashEnabled": true,
  "callerSelectedTargetEnabled": false,
  "callerSelectedRpcEnabled": false,
  "paymentExecutionEnabled": false,
  "walletAccessEnabled": false,
  "signingEnabled": false,
  "transactionSubmissionEnabled": false,
  "retryExecutionEnabled": false,
  "actionExecutionEnabled": false
}
```

`privacy` is exactly:

```json
{
  "transactionHashTransport": "public_url_query",
  "transactionHashMayAppearInPlatformLogs": true,
  "applicationPersistenceEnabled": false
}
```

`limitations` is exactly:

```json
{
  "intendedX402TermsProven": false,
  "httpDeliveryProven": false,
  "businessEffectProven": false,
  "retrySafetyProven": false
}
```

### Status semantics

- `confirmed`: exactly one finalized native-USDC EIP-3009
  `AuthorizationUsed` event immediately followed by its matching `Transfer` event
  was observed under unanimous configured-source policy.
- `multiple`: more than one qualifying finalized event pair was observed. No
  intended payment or duplicate-payment conclusion is inferred.
- `pending_finality`: the receipt was observed but is not yet at the shared
  finalized anchor.
- `not_observed`: the configured sources did not return a receipt at this
  observation snapshot. This does not prove absence; the transaction may be
  pending or unmined.
- `not_eip3009_usdc`: a receipt was observed without a qualifying adjacent
  native-USDC EIP-3009 event pair.
- `reverted`: a reverted receipt was observed. No event-pair success is claimed.
- `contradiction`: configured observations failed a fixed source-agreement,
  network identity, code identity, canonicality, or structural evidence rule.
  No transaction claim is made.

Provider/configuration failures are not transaction verdicts. Invalid requests
return HTTP 400, unsupported methods return HTTP 405, request limits may return
HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`, and bounded upstream unavailability returns HTTP 503.
No raw provider error, provider URL, source name, calldata, or unrelated receipt
log is returned.

Finalized non-contradictory responses may be cached for 5 seconds. Pending or
unobserved responses may be cached for 1 second. Contradictions and failures are
not cached. Transaction hashes are public onchain identifiers and may appear in
browser, CDN, function, or provider request logs. The application does not
persist verifier requests or results.

## GET /api/health

Returns the fixed live, read-only operating configuration. It performs no Base
read for the health request itself. The response reports:

- service `x402-canary` and status `operational_read_only`;
- mode `live_base_transaction_verification`;
- Base mainnet, native USDC, two configured sources, unanimous policy, and shared
  finalized-anchor policy;
- legacy probe routes disabled and scheduled monitoring disabled;
- caller-selected RPC disabled;
- wallet, signing, transaction submission, payment execution, retry execution,
  and action execution disabled.

## GET /api/evidence-status

Returns sanitized release metadata generated by the deployed source. It does not
read a private journal, artifact store, manifest, attestation, wallet, or RPC
endpoint. The live-verifier contract in this response pins:

- schema `0.1` and scope `transaction_only`;
- Base mainnet and native Base USDC;
- two configured sources with unanimous policy;
- shared-finalized-anchor finality;
- caller-selected RPC disabled;
- caller-selected transaction-hash lookup and fixed-source Base verification
  enabled;
- scheduled public outbound monitoring disabled;
- every execution capability disabled.

The release also describes the four bounded evidence layers and nine deterministic
shadow-runner classifications from core commit
`3ead8680d764ecbafe0739865f3789f8928f0fa6`. Those classifications remain evidence
method documentation; the public transaction route does not evaluate an expected
x402 intent or business effect.

## Disabled routes

- `/api/trust`: disabled and gone.
- `/api/preflight`: disabled and gone.

There is no public operation execution, authorization creation, signing,
transaction submission, payment, retry, action directive, arbitrary URL fetch,
arbitrary RPC method, arbitrary RPC origin, wallet connection, private evidence
upload, scheduled monitor, webhook, or background action.
